newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX hits fourth successive high.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX hits fourth successive high.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange's index rose to its fourth successive high on Tuesday, bucking the bearish trend of European markets, which moved lower ahead of the FOMC meeting, traders said.
"The Hungarian market seemed not to react to what happened on foreign markets," said Gregory Osztrovszky of Gog Securities.
The BUX index finished at 3,863.11 points, up 27.16.
Chemicals firm TVK played a major role in pushing the index higher. In active trade it extended its recent gains and rose to a new high of 1,745 forints, before closing at 1,725, up 25.

Another stock pushing the index up was holding company Csopak which joined TVK in rising to a new record high of 1,240 forints after East European Food Fund bought an over 30 percent stake in the company.
"The price rise was obviously the result of the purchase," one trader said.

Tuesday's spot share turnover of 1.34 billion forints remained below Monday's 1.64 billion, reflecting the fact that many investors either took a wait-and-see stance ahead of the Fed meeting or began to unwind their positions preparing for the Christmas, traders said.
Despite today's shrugging off of the world trend, Osztrovszky said the bourse will follow other exchanges soon.
"The Dow Jones opened lower -- I think the Hungarian market will react to that," he said.

One sign that the market may come down was the mixed picture for leading stocks, while some investors are deciding to sell stocks to lock in profits on what has been one of the fastest growing bourse in 1996, Osztrovszky said.
Elsewhere on the market the pharmaceuticals shares were little changed, while bank and hotel stocks were steady to firmer in meagre turnover.
Pharma stock Egis slipped five forints to end at 8,780 forints, Richter closed at 8,930, up 30, while Human ended at 2,620, up 20.

OTP Bank put up five forints to close at 2,690, just below the day's peak of 2,695, while volatile Inter-Europa Bank leapt 700 forints to finish at 36,200 forints, well below the day's peak of 38,000.
Hotelier Danubius ended at 3,695 forints, up 30, while the market's other hotel paper Eravis closed unchanged at 4,300.
